punchline: A ten-year-old with a bird report due tomorrow and three months already gone got one sentence from his father: bird by bird.
thirty_sec: Anne Lamott's brother was ten, with a report on birds due the next day and three months already gone. He sat at the table next to binder paper, pencils and unopened bird books, close to tears. Their father put an arm around him and said, 'Bird by bird, buddy. Just take it bird by bird.' Lamott uses that line to teach writers to work in small pieces, and she keeps a one-inch picture frame on her desk as a reminder.
